t.E161b.agn: EFSA set the ADI at 1 mg/kg body weight; in 2012 it reported that in some countries this limit may be exceeded by foods and the additive together in high-consuming children, but not in adults.
t.E161b.body: It is absorbed in the small intestine together with fats and bile salts and enters the bloodstream in free form. Its molecule is not cleaved, so it is not converted into vitamin A; oxidation of its hydroxyl groups gives products that are readily excreted. In humans, about 45% of a single oral dose of labelled lutein was excreted in the faeces and 10% in the urine within the first 48 hours.
t.E161b.eff.0.t: Foods and the additive together may exceed the daily limit
t.E161b.prod: Obtained by solvent extraction from plants such as marigold.
t.E161b.pw.0: According to EFSA, the daily intake limit may be exceeded in children who consume a lot of this dye.
t.E161b.regx.0: ADI 1 mg/kg; may be exceeded in high-consuming children in some countries.
t.E161b.summary: A yellow carotenoid found in marigold and green leafy vegetables. Used in confectionery, drinks and milk-based desserts.
t.E161b.what: Gives a yellow colour. Lutein also occurs naturally in green leafy vegetables.
